title.narrative: Provision of Emergency and Inclusive WASH Services for Drought Affected and Hard to Reach Populations in Tayeeglow District, Bakool Region

description.narrative: ltpgtThe humanitarian situation in Tayeeglow, Bakool Region, continues to deteriorate amid overlapping climatic and conflict‑related shocks. Recurrent drought, food insecurity, and displacement have severely strained access to life‑saving services, particularly safe water, sanitation, and hygiene. Findings from the Rapid WASH Assessment conducted by Action Against Hunger (ACF) and SAMA confirm that latrine coverage remains critically low, water sources are largely unsafe and unreliable, and hygiene supplies are almost entirely absent.lt/pgtltpgtRecognized by the Somalia Humanitarian Fund (SHF) as one of five high‑priority districts under the 2025 Reserve Allocation, Tayeeglow has been allocated USD 2.3 million to address urgent needs. The district’s severe WASH‑related vulnerabilities heighten public health risks, especially among internally displaced persons (IDPs), rural poor, women, children, the elderly, and persons with disabilities (PwDs)ltbrgtTo respond to these urgent needs, Salama Medical Agency (SAMA) proposes a 8-month standalone WASH intervention that will reach approximately 14,118 individuals (including 2824 men, 3,812 women, 3,247 boys, and 4,235 girls, as well as people with disabilities and other vulnerable groups) across Tiyeglow and surrounding hard to reach villages. The project will deliver lifesaving and sustainable WASH activities, that comprise the following:ltbrgt Restoring safe water access: SAMA will rehabilitate two public boreholes in underserved rural villages (Sinai and Biyooley). The water points will be equipped with solar‑powered pumps, elevated tanks, gender‑sensitive distribution kiosks, and water troughs, supported by water quality monitoring and household‑level chlorination. In addition, four shallow wells will be rehabilitated through desilting, construction of aprons, and installation of Afrodev hand pumps. Gender‑balanced water management committees will be trained to oversee functionality and ensure sustainability. All rehabilitation works will be carried out in line with the Somalia WASH Clusters Toolkit for Small‑Scale Water Supply Systems, ensuring adherence to sectoral standards, technical quality, and long‑term sustainability.ltbrgt Expanding emergency sanitation: The project will construct 100 flood resistant communal latrines, with at least 15% adapted for people with disabilities (15 units). Each latrine will include a handwashing facility and solar lighting to ensure privacy and reduce GBV risks, particularly for women and girls at night. Sitting and design will be informed by protection assessments and community consultations, with sanitation materials distributed for ongoing maintenance.ltbrgt Promoting inclusive hygiene and risk communication: SAMA will deploy 10 trained hygiene promoters and 4 community mobilizers to conduct structured door to door visits and community dialogues. Messaging will emphasize hand hygiene, IPC, latrine care, safe water handling, menstrual hygiene management (MHM), and PSEA awareness, using Somalia WASH Cluster approved materials. Hygiene kits including buckets, jerry cans, soap, aqua tabs, and sanitary pads will be distributed to 1000 vulnerable households, while designated sites will receive sanitation tools for solid waste control and community clean up campaigns. ltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtThe project will establish Complaint and Feedback Mechanisms (CFMs), ensure inclusive targeting, and involve women, PwDs, and minority leaders in design, monitoring, and delivery. Field teams will coordinate with WASH, Protection, ABC platforms, and local authorities for convergence. Guided by recent ACF/SAMA assessments, SHF priorities, and protection monitoring, the intervention upholds Sphere standards, reducing WASH‑related risks and contributing to SHF’s 2025 commitment in underserved districts, including Tayeeglow.ltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgt
